_about: Toggle Link Chain (YF5143), 16 candidate concepts for 15 high-CTR Meta ads (4 Nov 2026). Each must pass the founder's one-second prop test (REDO43.md): the prop is where the piece is worn or kept, a true look-alike of its shape, name or material, or nothing but the product. Lines under seven words, Naira voice: a real noun, then a turn.
product: Toggle Link Chain, Rs 1,199 (compare-at Rs 2,900), 79 in stock. 50 cm, 4 mm open paperclip links (about 4 x 11 mm), gold tone (18k PVD on surgical stainless steel). Clasp about 15 mm: a thick polished spring-gate ring with a push-pin nub, and a short straight pave bar of tiny clear stones on the other chain end. Worn with the clasp at the front or the side. Ships in the Naira gift box; free insured shipping; COD on serviceable pincodes; Buy 2 for 10% off, Buy 3 for 20% off, automatic in the bag.
evidence: Naira ads above 4% CTR share: a familiar Indian thing that looks like the piece (anaar, kesar, rangoli); a line that names it and turns it; 'X, not Y' craft truths; one piece on one ground with air; Stories beat Feed; the best seller had no words on the picture. Generic occasion lines stayed under 2.2%. Toggle history (lifetime): 'Paperclip, promoted.' 7.32% on 41 impressions; VK Story 4.38% on 160; 'Out by noon.' (sunglasses) 1.64% on 366; VK fork Feed 2.15% on 465.

concepts.line: Only one of these is Rs 1,199.
concepts.alt: Spot the one that isn't stationery.
concepts.picture: Top-down, the frame filled edge to edge with a dense heap of ordinary silver steel office paperclips on a pale blush desk; through the middle runs one gold paperclip chain, its ring clasp visible. The paperclips are about three times the length of a chain link, so the necklace reads finer.
concepts.why: Builds on the best Toggle number (Paperclip, promoted. 7.3%). A hunt keeps the thumb still; gold against silver pops.

concepts.picture: Extreme close-up of the clasp worn at the front on the upper breastbone, the ring a fifth of the frame wide, the pave bar catching a hard pin-point of light; the two strands climb out of frame. No face.
concepts.why: One piece, one ground, all detail: the click is to see it closer. Teaches the front-clasp way to wear it.

concepts.line: The clasp? It's at the front.
concepts.picture: Two panels: top, the nape of a neck with hair up, plain links and no clasp; bottom, the same chain from the front, the ring and bar sitting on the breastbone.
concepts.why: Opens a question the first panel cannot answer; the second answers it. Panels read in a second.

concepts.picture: Chocolate-brown ribbed knit turtleneck, cropped below the chin, the chain worn over it with the clasp at the front, low winter sun.
concepts.why: November to February in the north; the look people already save on Pinterest. Gold on brown is high contrast.

concepts.line: Fasten it where you can see it.
concepts.picture: Two hands at the front of the chest fastening the clasp, the bar going into the ring, cropped below the chin.
concepts.why: Everyone has fought a clasp behind their neck. A practical promise the listing supports (worn at the front).

concepts.line: Actual size. Hold it to your collarbone.
concepts.picture: The C02 frame scaled so the ring is 15 mm on a typical phone screen (about 249 px on the 1080 Story); a small 15 mm scale mark.
concepts.why: Novel and true: people hold the phone up, which is dwell, then tap to buy. Removes the size doubt.

concepts.picture: Top-down on a saturated cobalt ground, the chain laid in joined-up handwriting spelling 'hi', the ring clasp sitting on top of the i as its dot; hard sun, crisp shadow.
concepts.why: Jewellery that writes a word stops a scroll; the ad literally says hi. Product only, no prop.

concepts.picture: The chain hanging from two fingertips in hard low light; on the plaster wall behind, its shadow is huge and crisp, every paperclip link drawn large.
concepts.why: A look-twice image with nothing but the product and light; the line names the contrast.

concepts.picture: A small ceramic catch-all dish by the front door: a set of brass house keys on a split ring and the chain beside them, its ring echoing the key ring.
concepts.why: The three things you check before you leave; says everyday without saying everyday.

concepts.line: This one doesn't go in the almirah.
concepts.picture: The steel almirah where Indian families lock jewellery away, its brass key in the lock, the chain hanging from the key's ring.
concepts.why: Good jewellery gets saved for occasions; this one is for every day. A real Indian noun turned.

concepts.picture: A school-party paper-loop chain in pastel strips on a blush ground, its last loop handing over to the gold chain, which carries on in links of the same shape.
concepts.why: Everyone made one in school; the shape is the same. The founder kept a paper chain for a chain before.

concepts.picture: Split frame: the same crew-neck white tee, cropped below the chin, plain on the left, with the chain and front clasp on the right.
concepts.why: Before/after is the fastest read in a feed; shows the piece doing its one job.

concepts.picture: A weathered blue wooden door with an old brass ring-and-chain latch (kundi); the gold chain hangs from the latch ring.
concepts.why: A ring and a bar through it is how old doors shut; the shape rhyme is real and nostalgic.

concepts.picture: The open Naira gift box, the chain coiled inside, the lid leaning beside it, a blank kraft tag.
concepts.why: A sibling truth every Indian family knows; speaks to the buyer who is not the wearer, including men.

concepts.picture: Worn over a crisp white cotton kurta's open neckline, clasp at the front, morning light.
concepts.why: 'The everyday chain' in the words people use; tests a Hinglish line against English ones.

concepts.picture: The chain alone, pooled on blush silk, the clasp on top, the Buy 2 / Buy 3 chip large.
concepts.why: A hard reason to buy now (S3_11 any-three ad scored near the top of the 20).
